learning_outcomes.text: Evaluate and thermodynamically size energy conversion systems, particularly those commonly used in industrial plants (cc4).
Recognize and classify the main energy systems, describe their operating principles, and assess plant performance based on energy balances and fluid machinery characteristics (cc4).
Identify algorithmic approaches and use databases for energy system evaluation and sizing (cc9).
Apply the principles of thermodynamics to energy systems described by main thermodynamic cycles.
Correctly interpret thermodynamic diagrams.
Select and apply appropriate analytical and modelling methods for thermal power plants and energy conversion systems.
Assess the energy and environmental performance of conversion plants.
Demonstrate independent judgement in preparing and selecting solution methods for thermodynamic analysis of energy systems (ag1, ag4, ag5).
Present a specific topic covered during lectures, encouraging independent ability to argue the answer (ag5).
Communicate through graphical and tabular representation of thermodynamic cycles, systems and results (ac2, ac3).
Communicate specific issues relating to energy systems clearly and rigorously, highlighting analysis criteria (ac1, ac2).
Develop models of energy conversion systems independently (ap1).
Gather further bibliographic information and develop the ability to solve problems and undertake simple projects (ap2, ap3).
Knowledge and understanding of thermodynamics applied to energy systems and of fluid-dynamic phenomena as well as models capable of representing them.
Knowledge of systems and machines for the production and conversion of energy, with particular reference to turbomachinery and industrial combustion equipment.
Understanding the role of different energy technologies in ensuring the environmental and economic sustainability of production.

Knowledge and understanding of information technology including the role they play in supporting design. Understanding the organization of information in databases and computer design to support processes.

Applying knowledge and understanding related to analytical modelling and experimental methods to design, analyze and test fluid machines, thermal motors and energy conversion systems. This includes: the application of design criteria for technical and thermos-technical plants, fluid and energy distribution; the application of thermodynamic principles to simple systems; the understanding of the main thermodynamic cycles and the reading of thermal diagrams; the identification of significant heat transmission mechanisms for engineering applications; the analysis and functional design of equipment of mechanical interest such as turbomachinery, energy conversion systems and internal combustion engines; the evaluation of the energy, economic and environmental performance of fluid, thermal and oleo-dynamic machinery.
Graphic representation and communication (drafting of diagrams, graphs and tables).

Provide an in-depth analysis on different topics related to Energy Engineering, like components design through advanced thermo-fluid-dynamics aspects and energy systems characterization, in the form of energy storage systems.
Provide the student with the knowledge and the methodologies necessary to face and solve, in a proper way, problems related to the treated aspects.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to renewable Energy Systems and ORC
Energy system modeling systems using a modular object-oriented approach
Application to conventional and innovative systems
Energy Conversion national and worldwide scenario
Combustion Process: Fundamentals; specific applications for Energy Conversion plants
Steam PowerPlants: thermodynamic features and components descriptions. Performance
Gas Turbine PowerPlants: thermodynamic features and components descriptions. Performance
Reciprocating internal combustion engines. Ideal and limit cycle for four-stroke spark ignition and ignition for compression. Real cycle and performance
Cogeneration and combined cycles. Thermodynamic advantages of cogeneration: analysis parameters and regulatory overview
Cogeneration plants with steam turbines, gas turbines and volumetric heat engines
Combined gas-steam cycles. Operating principles and types
Rankine cycles with ORC organic fluids and overview of the main solutions for the exploitation of renewable energy
Numerical tools for modeling energy systems
Examples of conventional and cooling system
Simplified design method for GT cooled components
CAES (Compressed Energy Storage Systems): principle, examples and efficiency improvement methods
Hydrogen-based energy storage: principle and comparison between methodologies
Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engine: thermodynamic features and components descriptions. Performance
Combined Cycles and Cogeneration: thermodynamic features and components descriptions. Performance
Organic Rankine Cycles for Heat recovery at low temperature. Introduction to main energy systems for renewable energy sources exploitation
teaching_methods: Group practice on assigned projects with periodic revisions

assessment_methods.method: Review and assessment of written assignment (for Powerplant section)

assessment_rules: Students can take 3 intermediate tests; passing these gives direct access to the oral test and final vote. If intermediate tests are not taken or passed, students must pass a written test and then an oral test. For the M-Z partition, students may sit two mid-term exams, with an average mark of 10 or above to pass, leading to an oral exam. Failing or not sitting mid-term exams requires passing a comprehensive written test (minimum 14) to access the oral exam. Students must demonstrate at least sufficient knowledge of mathematical/physical modelling and energy components/systems.
